Title: Attention Is All You Need
Summary: Introduced the Transformer architecture, which replaced recurrence and convolutions with multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward layers. This architecture enabled massive parallelization during training, improved long-range dependency modeling in sequences, and became the foundation for modern large language models and many downstream NLP and multimodal systems.

Title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
Summary: Proposed BERT, a technique for pre-training deep bidirectional transformer encoders using masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction. BERT demonstrated large gains on many NLP benchmarks by providing strong contextual representations that could be fine-tuned for diverse downstream tasks, reshaping transfer learning in NLP.

Title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
Summary: Presented GPT-3, a very large autoregressive transformer language model with 175 billion parameters that exhibited strong few-shot, one-shot, and zero-shot generalization abilities. The work showed that scale of model parameters and pretraining data can drastically change capabilities, enabling many tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.

Title: ResNet: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
Summary: Introduced residual connections to enable training of extremely deep convolutional neural networks by learning residual functions instead of direct mappings. Residual networks improved gradient flow, reduced training difficulties for deep nets, and achieved state-of-the-art results on ImageNet, influencing many subsequent architectures.

Title: AlexNet: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Summary: Demonstrated that deep convolutional networks trained on large GPU clusters could drastically outperform traditional computer vision pipelines on large-scale image classification benchmarks. AlexNet popularized ReLU activations, dropout, data augmentation, and GPU training practices that accelerated the deep learning era for vision.

Title: VGG: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
Summary: Studied the effect of depth in convolutional networks by using small 3x3 filters and stacking many layers, showing that deeper networks can yield improved recognition performance when trained carefully. VGG models became a simple and influential baseline for many vision tasks.

Title: Inception (GoogLeNet): Going Deeper with Convolutions
Summary: Introduced the Inception module that combined filters of multiple sizes in parallel and used dimensionality reduction to manage computation. The architecture allowed deeper and wider networks with efficient computation and paved the way for scaling convolutional nets in resource-constrained settings.

Title: Word2Vec: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
Summary: Introduced efficient neural network models (skip-gram and CBOW) to learn dense word embeddings from large corpora, capturing semantic and syntactic relationships via vector arithmetic. Word2Vec embeddings became central to many NLP systems and inspired later contextual representation approaches.

Title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
Summary: Proposed GloVe, a global log-bilinear regression model that leveraged aggregated global word-word co-occurrence statistics to produce vector representations of words. GloVe provided robust, efficient embeddings that combined global corpus statistics with local context windows for improved semantics.

Title: FastText: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
Summary: Presented FastText, which improved word embeddings by modeling subword information (character n-grams), allowing robust representations for rare and morphologically rich words. FastText also included an efficient text classification approach and became popular for resource-constrained and multilingual settings.

Title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
Summary: Developed the sequence-to-sequence framework using encoder-decoder neural networks for mapping input sequences to output sequences, facilitating tasks like machine translation and summarization. The approach helped popularize end-to-end neural methods for many sequence transformation problems.

Title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (Bahdanau et al.)
Summary: Introduced attention mechanisms within sequence-to-sequence models to allow decoders to focus on relevant encoder states during generation. This alignment mechanism improved translation quality and inspired the broad adoption of attention in many sequence modeling tasks.

Title: LSTM: Long Short-Term Memory
Summary: Proposed the LSTM recurrent unit with gating mechanisms to address vanishing and exploding gradients in RNNs, enabling learning of long-range dependencies in sequential data. LSTMs became foundational models for speech recognition, language modeling, and many time-series tasks before transformers gained prominence.

Title: GRU: Gated Recurrent Unit
Summary: Introduced the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) as a simpler gating mechanism alternative to LSTM, combining reset and update gates for efficient sequence modeling. GRUs offered competitive performance with fewer parameters and became widely used in resource-constrained sequence learning tasks.

Title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
Summary: Presented Transformer-XL, which introduced recurrence and segment-level recurrence with adaptive computation to extend transformers' effective context length. The model improved long-context language modeling, addressing limitations of fixed-length context windows in standard transformers.

Title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding
Summary: Proposed XLNet, a generalized autoregressive pretraining method that integrated ideas from autoregressive and autoencoding approaches using permutation-based training. XLNet sought to capture bidirectional contexts while maintaining permutation-based factorization for improved language understanding.

Title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
Summary: Showed that BERT's performance could be improved substantially by removing next-sentence prediction, training with larger batches and data, and carefully tuning hyperparameters. RoBERTa emphasized the role of scale and training regimen in pretraining effectiveness.

Title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
Summary: Introduced parameter-reduction techniques for BERT-like models, including factorized embedding parameterization and cross-layer parameter sharing, to reduce memory usage and increase training speed while retaining strong performance on language tasks.

Title: T5: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
Summary: Formulated many NLP tasks in a unified text-to-text framework and scaled transformer-based models to pretrain on massive text corpora. T5 demonstrated that large, unified models could be fine-tuned to excel across diverse tasks by framing them consistently.

Title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators
Summary: Proposed ELECTRA, which pretrains transformers using a discriminator to detect replaced tokens generated by a small generator network. This approach yielded sample-efficient pretraining, allowing smaller compute budgets to reach competitive downstream performance compared to masked-language modeling.

Title: DistilBERT: A Smaller, Faster, Cheaper Version of BERT
Summary: Presented DistilBERT which used knowledge distillation to compress BERT models, producing smaller, faster models with comparable performance. DistilBERT aimed to make transformer-based models more accessible for production and edge scenarios through efficient compression techniques.

Title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
Summary: Introduced BART, a denoising autoencoder for sequence-to-sequence pretraining that combined bidirectional and autoregressive modeling, achieving strong results on text generation and comprehension tasks and enabling flexible fine-tuning for varied NLP objectives.

Title: GPT-2: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
Summary: Demonstrated that large-scale unsupervised language models could perform various NLP tasks through zero-shot and few-shot inference, and presented GPT-2, a large autoregressive transformer that generated coherent long-form text, sparking debates about model safety and release strategies.

Title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
Summary: Described PaLM, a large-scale language model trained with efficient routing and scaling strategies to improve few-shot performance and reasoning capabilities. The work investigated scaling laws and architecture choices that influence emergent capabilities in very large models.

Title: Chinchilla: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
Summary: Argued that many large language models were undertrained relative to their parameter counts and proposed scaling compute to balance model size and training tokens. Chinchilla provided practical guidance for training compute-optimal LLMs and showed improved sample-efficiency.

Title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
Summary: Presented LLaMA, a family of smaller but performant transformer models trained on curated corpora with careful pretraining recipes, demonstrating that competitive downstream performance can be achieved with more parameter-efficient models and data choices.

Title: OPT: Open Pretrained Transformer Models
Summary: Released OPT models to support research reproducibility by providing openly available transformer language models and training logs. The work allowed researchers to study scaling, capabilities, and risks of large language models with transparent checkpoints and evaluations.

Title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open Multilingual Language Model
Summary: Described the creation of a large multilingual open language model trained collaboratively across many institutions. BLOOM aimed to provide an open alternative to proprietary LLMs for multilingual research and to explore the social and technical implications of large-scale models.

Title: BigGAN: Large Scale GAN Training for High Fidelity Natural Image Synthesis
Summary: Details methods for scaling Generative Adversarial Networks to produce high-fidelity images by carefully tuning architecture, batch normalization, and training procedures. BigGAN demonstrated that larger capacity and careful regularization could yield realistic synthetic images.

Title: StyleGAN: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
Summary: Introduced a style-based generator architecture that allowed explicit control over image synthesis properties at different spatial scales, enabling high-quality and interpretable generation of faces and scenes. StyleGAN variants became widely used for generative tasks and creative applications.

Title: CycleGAN: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
Summary: Proposed CycleGAN, which enabled image-to-image translation without paired training data by enforcing cycle-consistency between mappings. This approach allowed style transfer, domain adaptation, and artistic transformations when aligned datasets were not available.

Title: Autoencoders and Variational Autoencoders (VAE)
Summary: Developed variational autoencoders which combine probabilistic latent variable modeling with neural networks to enable principled generation and representation learning. VAEs offer a framework for unsupervised learning with interpretable latent spaces and have been applied in generative modeling.

Title: Neural Style Transfer
Summary: Showed how deep convolutional feature representations can be used to transfer artistic style from one image onto the content of another, using optimization of image content and style losses derived from CNN activations. This work popularized creative uses of deep networks.
Topic: Computer Vision, Style Transfer, Deep Learning

Title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
Summary: Introduced the U-Net architecture with encoder-decoder structure and skip connections tailored for biomedical segmentation tasks with limited data. U-Net's design improved localization and feature reuse, making it a staple in medical image analysis and segmentation tasks.

Title: Mask R-CNN: Instance Segmentation
Summary: Extended Faster R-CNN with a parallel branch for predicting segmentation masks, enabling accurate instance-level segmentation along with bounding boxes and class labels. Mask R-CNN became a standard approach for many instance segmentation tasks in vision.
Topic: Computer Vision, Instance Segmentation, Deep Learning

Title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
Summary: Combined region proposal networks with Fast R-CNN to produce an end-to-end object detection pipeline that improved speed and accuracy. Faster R-CNN's integration of proposal generation and detection advanced object detection benchmarks and practical systems.
Topic: Computer Vision, Object Detection, Deep Learning

Title: YOLO: You Only Look Once — Real-Time Object Detection
Summary: Proposed a single-stage object detector that framed detection as a regression problem over bounding boxes and class probabilities, enabling real-time inference with good accuracy. YOLO variants have been widely used in applications requiring speed-sensitive detection.

Title: SSD: Single Shot MultiBox Detector
Summary: Presented SSD, a single-stage detection approach using multi-scale feature maps for detecting objects at different sizes. SSD balanced detection accuracy and inference speed, making it practical for embedded and mobile visual systems.
Topic: Computer Vision, Object Detection, Deep Learning

Title: MobileNet: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications
Summary: Introduced depthwise separable convolutions to drastically reduce computation and parameters for convolutional networks, enabling efficient models for mobile and embedded devices while retaining respectable accuracy on vision tasks.

Title: EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks
Summary: Proposed a compound model scaling method to balance depth, width, and resolution in convolutional networks, achieving strong accuracy with efficient computation. EfficientNet families became go-to models for performance/efficiency trade-offs in vision tasks.

Title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
Summary: Introduced batch normalization to stabilize and accelerate training of deep neural networks by normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, allowing higher learning rates and improved regularization. BatchNorm became a standard component in modern deep architectures.

Title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
Summary: Proposed dropout, a regularization technique that randomly drops units during training to prevent co-adaptation of features. Dropout improved generalization across many neural architectures and remains a common regularizer in practice.

Title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
Summary: Presented Adam, an adaptive learning rate optimization algorithm that combined ideas from momentum and RMSProp, providing efficient convergence with minimal hyperparameter tuning. Adam quickly became a default optimizer for many neural network applications.

Title: SGD with Momentum and Nesterov Accelerated Gradient
Summary: Studied momentum-based acceleration of stochastic gradient descent, including Nesterov's accelerated gradient variants, which improved convergence speed by incorporating an estimate of future gradients. These techniques remain central to deep learning optimization practices.

Title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
Summary: Described XGBoost, a scalable and efficient implementation of gradient boosting decision trees with regularization, sparsity-aware algorithms, and parallelization. XGBoost achieved state-of-the-art results on many tabular tasks and competitions, becoming a go-to method for structured data.
Topic: Ensemble Methods, Gradient Boosting, Structured Data

Title: LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
Summary: Proposed LightGBM which used histogram-based algorithms, leaf-wise tree growth, and optimizations to speed up gradient boosting on large datasets. LightGBM emphasized training efficiency and memory footprint for large-scale structured learning.
Topic: Ensemble Methods, Gradient Boosting, Structured Data

Title: CatBoost: Unbiased Boosting with Categorical Features Support
Summary: Introduced CatBoost, a gradient boosting library addressing categorical feature handling and target leakage through ordered boosting methods and encoders, improving performance on datasets with categorical variables without heavy preprocessing.
Topic: Ensemble Methods, Gradient Boosting, Structured Data

Title: SVM: Support Vector Machines
Summary: Established support vector machines, which find maximum-margin hyperplanes for classification using kernel methods to handle nonlinearly separable data. SVMs provided strong theoretical foundations for margin-based learning with broad applications in classification and regression.
Topic: Classical ML, Kernel Methods, Supervised Learning

Title: Random Forests
Summary: Introduced Random Forests, an ensemble of decision trees trained with bootstrap aggregation and random feature selection to reduce variance and overfitting. Random Forests provided robust performance across many tasks and became a staple algorithm for tabular data.

Title: AdaBoost: A Short Introduction to Boosting
Summary: Presented AdaBoost, an influential boosting algorithm that adaptively reweights training examples to focus on hard-to-classify cases and combines weak learners into a strong ensemble, providing theoretical insights and practical utility in classification.

Title: t-SNE: Stochastic Neighbor Embedding for Visualization
Summary: Proposed t-SNE, a nonlinear dimensionality reduction technique that preserves local structure for high-dimensional data visualization, enabling meaningful 2D/3D embeddings for exploratory analysis though at higher computational cost for large datasets.

Title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction
Summary: Introduced UMAP, which provided faster, scalable dimensionality reduction for visualization and downstream tasks by modeling data manifolds via fuzzy simplicial sets and optimizing low-dimensional embeddings, often yielding meaningful global and local structure preservation.

Title: PCA: Principal Component Analysis (Classical)
Summary: Described principal component analysis as a linear dimensionality reduction method that finds orthogonal directions explaining maximal variance in data. PCA is a foundational technique for preprocessing, visualization, and noise reduction across many domains.

Title: t5-small etc (Tokenization and Preprocessing advances)
Summary: Work on tokenization, subword segmentation, and preprocessing improved how models represent text input, enabling better handling of rare words, multilingual corpora, and efficient input encoding. Methods like byte-pair encoding and sentencepiece became standard in model pipelines.

Title: Neural ODEs: Continuous-Depth Models
Summary: Introduced Neural Ordinary Differential Equations which treat transformations in deep networks as continuous-time dynamical systems, enabling adaptive computation, memory-efficient backpropagation, and new modeling perspectives linking differential equations with deep learning.
Topic: Continuous Models, Differential Equations, Deep Learning

Title: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN)
Summary: Proposed GCNs for semi-supervised learning on graph-structured data by generalizing convolutions to graphs using spectral or spatial message-passing operations. GCNs enabled powerful representations for nodes, graphs, and relational data tasks across many domains.

Title: GraphSAGE: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
Summary: Introduced GraphSAGE which enabled inductive node embedding learning by sampling and aggregating neighbor features, allowing representation learning that generalized to previously unseen nodes and large-scale graphs with efficient neighborhood sampling.

Title: GAT: Graph Attention Networks
Summary: Presented graph attention mechanisms to compute node representations by attending over neighbors with learned attention weights, improving expressivity and performance on graph tasks where neighbor importance varies, and combining attention with message passing frameworks.

Title: DeepWalk: Online Learning of Social Representations
Summary: Introduced DeepWalk which learned latent representations of graph nodes by sampling random walks and applying skip-gram style embedding learning, connecting language modeling approaches to graph representation learning and inspiring subsequent node embedding methods.

Title: node2vec: Scalable Feature Learning for Networks
Summary: Presented node2vec, which used biased random walks to explore neighborhoods and learn node embeddings balancing homophily and structural equivalence, providing flexible control over embedding behavior for downstream graph tasks.

Title: Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNN)
Summary: Formalized message passing frameworks for graph neural networks where nodes iteratively aggregate messages from neighbors, providing a unified paradigm for many graph architectures and enabling diverse tasks from chemistry to social network analysis.

Title: Siamese Networks for One-Shot Learning
Summary: Proposed siamese architectures that learn similarity metrics between pairs of inputs for one-shot and few-shot learning scenarios. These models improved tasks like face verification and metric learning by learning embeddings optimized for matching rather than classification alone.

Title: Matching Networks for One-Shot Learning
Summary: Developed matching networks that used attention over a support set for one-shot classification, combining metric learning with episodic training to improve generalization for few-shot tasks and inspire meta-learning approaches.

Title: Prototypical Networks
Summary: Introduced prototypical networks which represent each class by a prototype computed as the mean embedding of its support examples, achieving simple and effective few-shot classification with distance-based prediction rules and scalable episodic training.

Title: MAML: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning
Summary: Introduced MAML, an optimization-based meta-learning algorithm that finds initial model parameters which can be quickly adapted to new tasks with few gradient steps, enabling fast adaptation and improved performance on few-shot learning benchmarks.

Title: Reinforcement Learning: DQN (Deep Q-Networks)
Summary: Combined deep neural networks with Q-learning to learn value functions directly from high-dimensional inputs like raw pixels, enabling agents to learn control policies that beat human benchmarks in Atari games and spurring deep reinforcement learning research.

Title: AlphaGo: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search
Summary: Combined supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and Monte Carlo Tree Search to create an agent capable of defeating top Go players, demonstrating the power of combining deep learning with search-based planning in complex combinatorial games.

Title: AlphaZero: A General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm That Masters Chess, Shogi and Go
Summary: Showed that tabula-rasa self-play reinforcement learning with a unified neural network and Monte Carlo Tree Search could master complex board games without domain-specific heuristics, illustrating generality and high performance of deep RL in strategic games.

Title: MuZero: Mastering Go, Chess, Shogi and Atari without rules
Summary: Presented MuZero which learns a model of the environment's dynamics implicitly while planning with MCTS, enabling mastery of games without access to explicit rules, and combining model-based and model-free learning strengths effectively.

Title: PPO: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
Summary: Introduced PPO, a simple and reliable policy gradient method balancing sample efficiency and stability via clipped surrogate objectives. PPO became widely adopted in RL for its practical performance and ease of tuning across varied environments.

Title: SAC: Soft Actor-Critic
Summary: Presented Soft Actor-Critic, an off-policy actor-critic algorithm that optimizes a stochastic policy with an entropy term to encourage exploration, delivering stable learning and strong performance on continuous control benchmarks.

Title: A3C: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning
Summary: Proposed asynchronous actor-critic methods to stabilize and speed up RL training by leveraging multiple parallel environments, reducing correlation in updates and improving exploration via independent actor learners.

Title: TRPO: Trust Region Policy Optimization
Summary: Introduced TRPO, which constrained policy updates within trust regions to ensure stable policy improvements and reliable performance gains in policy gradient methods, informing later practical algorithms like PPO.

Title: REINFORCE: Policy Gradient Methods for Reinforcement Learning
Summary: Developed foundational policy gradient algorithms where gradients of expected returns are directly estimated using sampled trajectories, forming the basis of modern policy optimization methods and actor-critic variants.

Title: AlphaFold: Highly Accurate Protein Structure Prediction
Summary: Described AlphaFold, a deep learning system for predicting protein 3D structures from amino acid sequences with unprecedented accuracy, combining geometric insights, attention mechanisms, and evolutionary information; a milestone for computational biology and structural prediction.

Title: NeRF: Neural Radiance Fields for Novel View Synthesis
Summary: Introduced neural radiance fields which learn continuous volumetric scene representations from images enabling high-quality novel view synthesis and relighting. NeRFs combined differentiable rendering with deep scene representation learning for photorealistic 3D reconstruction.

Title: SimCLR: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
Summary: Presented SimCLR, which uses large-batch contrastive learning with aggressive data augmentation and a projection head to learn useful visual representations without labels, demonstrating that large-scale contrastive pretraining can rival supervised representations.
Topic: Self-Supervised Learning, Contrastive Learning, Computer Vision

Title: MoCo: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
Summary: Proposed MoCo, which maintains a dynamic dictionary with a momentum-updated encoder to enable contrastive learning with manageable memory and stable keys, facilitating effective unsupervised visual representation learning across large datasets.

Title: BYOL: Bootstrap Your Own Latent — Self-Supervised Learning without Negative Examples
Summary: Introduced BYOL, a self-supervised learning method that avoids explicit negative pairs by using momentum encoders and target networks, achieving strong representation learning performance and challenging assumptions about contrastive negatives.

Title: Barlow Twins: Self-Supervised Learning via Redundancy Reduction
Summary: Presented Barlow Twins, which learns representations by decorrelating components of paired representations and reducing redundancy, providing an alternative objective for self-supervised learning that focuses on information preservation without negatives.

Title: DeiT: Data-efficient Image Transformers
Summary: Showed that vision transformers could be trained efficiently on ImageNet-scale datasets using knowledge distillation from convolutional teachers, enabling competitive performance with smaller data regimes and introducing efficient training practices for ViT models.

Title: Vision Transformer (ViT): An Image is Worth 16x16 Words
Summary: Adapted transformer architectures to vision by splitting images into patches treated as tokens and applying standard transformer encoders. ViT demonstrated that pure transformer models can reach or surpass CNN performance when trained on large datasets.
Topic: Vision Transformers, Computer Vision, Deep Learning

Title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
Summary: Introduced Swin Transformer, which applied shifted window attention to build hierarchical representations for vision tasks, enabling efficient computation and strong performance across detection and segmentation benchmarks, bridging locality and global attention.

Title: Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention
Summary: Presented Perceiver models that process arbitrary modalities using latent arrays and cross-attention, enabling scalable and modality-agnostic architectures for audio, images, and multimodal tasks while avoiding quadratic attention costs on raw inputs.

Title: Performer: Efficient Transformers with Favorable Attention
Summary: Proposed Performer, which used random feature methods to approximate softmax attention with linear complexity, allowing transformers to scale to longer sequences efficiently while retaining performant attention approximations.

Title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer
Summary: Introduced memory- and time-efficient transformer modifications such as locality-sensitive hashing attention and reversible layers to reduce memory footprint and computation, enabling training of very long sequences and larger models with constrained resources.

Title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
Summary: Proposed sparse attention patterns and sliding-window mechanisms to handle long documents efficiently, combining local and global attention to scale transformers to long inputs for NLP and document understanding tasks with improved memory characteristics.

Title: Linformer: Self-Attention with Linear Complexity
Summary: Suggested low-rank projections of attention matrices to reduce the complexity of self-attention from quadratic to linear, enabling scaling to longer sequences with reduced computation and memory, while empirically preserving performance on many tasks.

Title: MLP-Mixer: An All-MLP Architecture for Vision
Summary: Showed that architectures based solely on multi-layer perceptrons with token-mixing and channel-mixing MLPs could achieve competitive vision performance, challenging assumptions that convolutions or self-attention are strictly necessary for strong image representations.

Title: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) Theory
Summary: Developed theoretical connections between infinitely wide neural networks and kernel methods, showing that training dynamics of wide networks can be approximated by kernel regression under certain limits and providing insights into optimization and generalization properties.

Title: Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
Summary: Proposed that dense, randomly initialized networks contain sub-networks (winning tickets) that, when trained in isolation, can reach comparable performance to the full network, inspiring research in pruning, sparsity, and efficient model training strategies.
Topic: Model Pruning, Sparse Networks, Training Efficiency

Title: Knowledge Distillation: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
Summary: Introduced knowledge distillation techniques where a smaller student model learns to mimic a larger teacher's softened outputs, enabling effective model compression and transfer of representational knowledge for efficient deployment.

Title: Quantization for Neural Networks
Summary: Research on quantization showed how to reduce model precision (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, binary) for weights and activations to lower memory and improve inference speed, exploring trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy critical for on-device and edge deployment.

Title: Prompting and In-Context Learning Studies
Summary: Series of works studied how large language models can be prompted with task descriptions and examples to perform various tasks without gradient updates, characterizing in-context learning dynamics, prompt engineering strategies, and limitations of prompt-based adaptation.

Title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
Summary: Introduced chain-of-thought prompting methods where language models are prompted to generate intermediate reasoning steps, improving performance on complex reasoning tasks by eliciting structured internal reasoning chains that enhance final answer correctness.

Title: Self-Play and Emergent Abilities in Scale
Summary: Research exploring emergent behaviors in large models and reinforcement settings found that scale, data diversity, and training regimes can lead to qualitatively new capabilities, from few-shot generalization to complex planning abilities, raising questions on predictability and evaluation.

Title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
Summary: Described empirical scaling laws that relate model performance to compute, parameters, and dataset size, enabling principled predictions for model scaling and guiding resource allocation for building higher-performing models.

Title: Multimodal Models: CLIP (Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training)
Summary: Proposed CLIP, which learns joint visual-text representations through contrastive objectives over image-caption pairs, enabling zero-shot transfer to many vision tasks and demonstrating the power of language supervision for visual representation learning.

Title: DALL·E: Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation
Summary: Demonstrated that transformer-based models trained on image-caption pairs could generate diverse and creative images from text prompts in a zero-shot manner, combining visual generation with language conditioning and opening new directions for generative multimodal AI.

Title: Stable Diffusion: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
Summary: Presented diffusion-based generative models operating in latent spaces that enable high-quality text-to-image synthesis with efficient sampling, demonstrating strong image fidelity, prompt conditioning, and practical usability for creative content generation at scale.

Title: Diffusion Models: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM)
Summary: Formalized diffusion-based generative modeling by learning reverse diffusion processes to map noise to data, achieving state-of-the-art sample quality in images and inspiring many extensions for conditional generation, audio synthesis, and latent-space diffusion variants.

Title: Guided Diffusion and Classifier-Free Guidance
Summary: Developed guidance techniques that steer diffusion sampling toward desired attributes or text prompts without relying on external classifiers, improving controllability and sample fidelity for conditional generation tasks across image and audio domains.

Title: Neural Architecture Search (NAS): NASNet
Summary: Applied automated architecture search to discover high-performing convolutional building blocks through reinforcement or evolutionary search, showing that automated design can produce architectures competitive with human-designed networks but requiring significant compute.

Title: DARTS: Differentiable Architecture Search
Summary: Introduced differentiable relaxation of architecture search spaces to enable gradient-based optimization of network architectures, drastically reducing compute for NAS and making automated model design more accessible and efficient for practitioners.

Title: EfficientDet: Scalable and Efficient Object Detection
Summary: Proposed EfficientDet which combined EfficientNet backbones with a compound scaling approach and BiFPN feature fusion to create a family of detectors that balance accuracy and computational cost, useful for resource-constrained detection systems.

Title: Attention Flow in Transformers: Interpretability Studies
Summary: Research on attention interpretability examined whether attention weights align with model explanations, probing the interpretability of transformer internals, causal roles of attention, and methods for attributing predictions to internal components for transparency.

Title: Adversarial Examples and Robustness
Summary: Series of works studying adversarial perturbations showed that neural networks can be vulnerable to small input changes that drastically alter outputs, prompting research into adversarial training, certified robustness, and defenses for secure ML deployment.

Title: Federated Learning: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
Summary: Introduced federated learning paradigms where models are trained across distributed devices holding local data without centralizing it, addressing privacy concerns and communication constraints via aggregation schemes and client-server protocols.

Title: Differential Privacy in Machine Learning
Summary: Applied differential privacy to learning algorithms to provide mathematical guarantees about privacy loss when models are trained on sensitive data, leading to algorithms that trade off utility and privacy for safe deployment on personal data.

Title: Fairness and Bias in Machine Learning
Summary: A body of research identified and measured social biases in ML systems, proposed fairness metrics, and introduced mitigation strategies spanning preprocessing, in-processing, and post-processing techniques to reduce disparate impacts across groups in deployed systems.
